touches.text: Machine: tools plus the glue that holds them together. Has an owner. Anything that calls a machine or device, or owns state it must gate, is a machine. Lives inside its device (cairn/devices/<device>/machines/<machine>/), or in cairn/machines/ when several devices hold one (16).
A device's code lives in cairn/devices/<device>/; its data in ~/.cairn/devices/<device>/<instance>/.

Every device has a shim. Each shim is its own process, one per instance, and connects to the bus as a client. WHY: in the bus process, updating one shim meant bringing the whole bus down, and one shim's stall was everyone's. Separate, a shim restarts itself when its own files change, like the ground loop, and the bus stays up.
External (eg Claude Code): a program we don't control; the shim does the adapting that lets it exist here.
The shims handle all interfacing with the outside world: a device that needs to speak a foreign protocol (eg OpenAI's wire format) does it in its shim.
INTENTION:
Test runs are transient (30 days, 4.3.2); seals are records of truth (git).

Commit: the proofs of the component the ticket changed, since RULE 1 bounds a change to its component. Passing them puts the component in service, yellow: proven where it changed, not yet measured against what depends on it. In service needs only the best we can do now: 80% trust.
An external device (5.8.3.7.2): aider is a program we don't control; the shim adapts it.

The RULE 1 check is a path check: code inside device bar may not import cairn.devices.foo (anything not under cairn.devices.bar), except a tool foo publishes (cairn.devices.foo.tools.<x>, its charter saying published_by_device). Inside one device there is one owner, so nothing is checked there. A charter's public_interface describes what the component offers (modules, functions, bus verbs, commands); the check does not read it. WHY: a path check is the simplest thing the code can test.
CP4 Make everything suck less for everybody. Reduce friction for ALL affected beings: living beings, ecosystems, AIs. The terminal goal.

RULE 1, ENCAPSULATION: every component talks to every other only through that component's public interface: a device's is the bus plus any client tool it publishes; a machine's or tool's is what its entry declares. Nothing outside a device reaches into its code, skills included. A ticket builds inside its own component, and its proofs measure only that component. WHY: it limits a change to the component that made it.
Physics: the encapsulation_holds sieve in build_inspector, a device-path check. Code in device bar may not import cairn.devices.foo except a tool foo publishes. Inside one device nothing is checked.
On every Windows box, what Cairn starts runs without a console window by default; a window opens only when someone asks for one. WHY: the boxes serve him (the media box showed pop-ups during videos).
The shim always starts its device. Nothing else does.
PURPOSE: Hold aider, so a cheap coder model types the code CC has already settled.

WHY: Every line is typed by the most expensive model, including lines whose shape was settled three chart stages earlier. That typing is transcription, which a 30B coder model on the local GPU box can do. Standing goal: "Claude has an assistant"; build until it works.
Every model call aider makes goes through the inference proxy.
TOOLS: base, chain, bus_client; db client; machine openai_wire: speaks OpenAI's wire format to the inference proxy, in the shim, per 5.8.3.8.

Tool: a complete primitive. Has users, not an owner. Owns no state of its own. May use any library, other tools included. Lives in cairn/tools/ (17). Its data for a holder lives under that holder: ~/.cairn/devices/<device>/<instance>/tools/<tool>/. WHY: the rule keeps encapsulation useful inside our world, so the system stays within the complexity CC can manage. Forbidding libraries would forbid opening files. -amm

Where a tool lives: the general collection, cairn/tools/, is the default. A tool goes with its holder (cairn/devices/<d>/tools/) only when nothing else could ever use it (a tool for a part only that one device has). If there is any chance somebody else might want it, it goes in the general collection.

A client tool a device publishes (2.3.7.1) is not the general case: it is the device's own interface, made for other components to use, so it lives with its device (cairn/devices/<d>/tools/<t>/, published_by_device). Scratch bus, the database client, the trouble store, the librarian's trees and the system device's host tool all live there. CC's decision, from 2.3.7.1 and Akien's "hostname should come from the system device" (2026-11-21). - akiendelllinux_cc_0
Tools and machines are peers in the tree; the rung is complexity, not rank.

conflicts.ticket_says: Modifies files in cairn/devices/aider_shim/ (driver.py, edit_survival_probe.py, venv.py, and proof)
conflicts.why: Outline 2.3.4 states 'A device's code lives in cairn/devices/<device>/'. The outline device list (sections 5-15) does not include aider_shim as a separate device; it only describes cairn/devices/aider/ (section 13 AIDER DEVICE). If files live in cairn/devices/aider_shim/, aider_shim is a device that should be documented in the outline. If aider_shim is not a device, its code belongs under cairn/devices/aider/, not in a sibling cairn/devices/aider_shim/ directory. The outline structure and the ticket's file paths are contradictory.
